text:
maria: pushing TICK-12345 from acme: customer reports p99 latency jumped to ~18s for text-generation endpoints since 02:10 UTC. They included request ids and a tiny repro. filing here so eng can triage. https://tickets.redwood/acme/12345

sam: looking. can you paste the sample req ids + region?

maria: req ids: r=fc3a2, r=fc3a9. region=us-west-2. stack traces link: https://obs.redwood/traces/trace.fc3a2 (shows long queue wait)

kevin: seeing same in metrics — ingress queue depth spike for host acme-prod-west at 02:08. p95 from 400ms->2.1s, p99 3.4s->18s. Worker pool error rates stable, CPU low. suggests admission/queueing backlog.

alex: tagging @sam — probable tenant hotpath causing head-of-line blocking. any recent deploys or model swaps for that tenant?

sam: no deploys in that window. checking admission controller logs now.

sre-bot: alert: ingress_queue_depth >= 200 for tenant=acme-prod-west at 2026-03-17T02:09:12Z (rule: queue-pressure-high)

kevin: admission controller is rejecting bursts but backlog shows many inflight waiting on a small subset of workers pinned to a gpu model variant. looks like imbalance + fairness config limiting concurrency per-worker.

maria: customer says they started a heavy batch job at 02:05 and then latency went bad for real-time traffic. they need immediate mitigation — they are seeing user-facing errors.

alex: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily raise tenant concurrency cap for acme-prod-west 2) enable priority routing for real-time keys 3) move batch job to low-priority queue or suggest backoff to customer

sam: roll it out. I'll bump concurrency and open a short-lived route override. running command:```rbacctl set-tenant-capacity --tenant acme --region us-west-2 --concurrency 20```

sam: and add route override:```redwood route update --tenant acme --env prod --priority real-time --weight 1.0```

kevin: applying now. also restarting 2 workers that appear stuck on large KV-caches:```kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/inference-worker-gpu-3 inference-worker-gpu-4```

sre-bot: action-log: tenant-capacity-change by sam at 02:18 UTC; route-override applied; worker restarts triggered.

sam: after changes p99 on that tenant dropped from 18s -> 1.6s within 40s. ingress queue depth down to normal. pushing notification to customer that we've applied a temporary unblock.

maria: customer confirmed improvement and reduced user errors. they will reschedule batch job for maintenance window.

alex: follow-ups: - add automatic tenant surge detection -> auto-increase soft concurrency for X mins - surface tenant-level busy signals in support UI - consider fairness sharding so single tenant batch doesn't monopolize specific worker variants

kevin: opened infra ticket INF-789 to implement auto-soft-scaling and fairness sharding. linking here: https://infra.redwood/INF-789

sam: left a temp playbook snippet in the runbook channel. snippet:```Mitigation steps for tenant queue surge:\n1) identify tenant and region\n2) bump tenant soft concurrency\n3) enable route priority override for real-time keys\n4) restart suspected stuck workers\n5) notify customer and monitor p99 for 10m\n```

maria: closing customer escalation after we get 10m stable. thanks all :thumbsup:

ticket-bot: TICK-12345 status changed -> RESOLVED by maria

kevin: retro note: we should add a quick support button to bump tenant soft limits (audited) to avoid handoffs for obvious surges.

alex: AGREED. I'll prioritise in next sprint.

maria: marking thread resolved internally, leaving links in ticket.
